newsitem.title: ITALY: Early 1997 Italian deficit data negative - report.
newsitem.headline: Early 1997 Italian deficit data negative - report.

text.p: Early 1997 data pointed to a worse-than-expected public sector deficit this year underlining the need for a hefty mini-budget, financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said in an unsourced report.
It said provisional Treasury figures indicated that without corrective measures the budget deficit would balloon to 76.5 trillion lire this year against a 62.5 trillion lire target.
This was assuming that the 1997 budget, which aims to cut 62.4 trillion lire off the deficit, would be entirely effective.

In order to tame accounts and reduce the ratio between the budget deficit and GDP to three percent, Prime Minister Romano Prodi will need to introduce a mini-budget worth at least 20 trillion lire, the paper said.

However the government might get some help from the European Commission. Italian newspapers have reported that Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi asked Brussels on Monday to re-classify Italian budget calculations.
